ruling: Owner ruling A, 2026-08-14 (the receipt pair) and the owner's follow-up ruling of the same day (the preimage lock), which together retire all three tx-field names. Both execute the owner's 2026-08-10 ruling that the tx-field chain dies before #579's single blueprint regeneration.
claim: The regenerated blueprint's (hub_oracle, field_preimage_certificate_policy_id) parameters are applied to user_events/tx_order_v1.mint, and all THREE dead tx-field entries — txOrderFieldPreimageSpend, txOrderFieldReceiptSpend and txOrderFieldReceiptMint — are removed from the positional deployment ABI vectors.
note: This is an identity REMOVAL from positional vectors, not a cleanup, and it is the FIRST removal in the deployment-manifest chain — every prior movement was append-only. DEPLOYMENT_MANIFEST_V1_CONTRACT_NAMES is ordered and its order IS the ABI, so dropping three entries renumbers every contract after them and moves the deployment-manifest id and every position-derived downstream identity. It is recorded here rather than left implicit in a diff because the value of a positional ABI is that every movement in it is enumerated with its cause. Every digest below was re-derived by running the gate, never copied from prose. EXECUTION HISTORY, kept because it is the honest record: the receipt pair was removed first under ruling A, which moved ABI-01 57->55; executing that surfaced the preimage lock as a third member of the same retirement, which was escalated rather than guessed at, and the owner then ruled it removed too, taking ABI-01 55->54. The intermediate digests are recorded as superseded, not erased.

whyTheEntriesWereDead.onchain: Commit df53dc6a7 (#587), executing the owner's 2026-08-10 ruling that 'the tx-field receipt chain dies before #579's single blueprint regeneration rather than being frozen into it', deleted THREE validators in one change: validators/user-events/tx-field-preimage-v1.ak, tx-field-receipt-v1.ak and tx-field-receipt-spend-v1.ak. Confirmed by `git log --diff-filter=D --name-only -- onchain/aiken/validators/user-events/`. Removing the three off-chain registrations completes off-chain what that commit did on-chain.
whyTheEntriesWereDead.parameters: #594 replaced the tx-order mint's two receipt parameters with the §8.6 certificate policy id.
whyTheEntriesWereDead.blueprint: The regenerated onchain/aiken/plutus.json (md5 b20c9a14a8fe445cdddbe5305b3857c1, 398 validators) declares none of `user_events/tx_field_preimage_v1.spend.spend`, `user_events/tx_field_receipt_v1.mint.mint` or `user_events/tx_field_receipt_spend_v1.spend.spend`, and declares `user_events/tx_order_v1.mint` with exactly two parameters: hub_oracle (aiken/crypto/ScriptHash) and field_preimage_certificate_policy_id (cardano/assets/PolicyId). Measured by sweeping all 36 blueprint-title string literals in midgard-contracts.ts against the blueprint: after the full removal, 35 of 35 resolve and 0 are missing.
whyTheEntriesWereDead.consequence: Until this change the load site resolved titles that no longer exist and applied a three-term parameter vector against a two-parameter declaration. `applyBlueprintDeclaredParams` is what kept that honest — it checks the application against the blueprint's declared parameters and fails by name rather than producing a wrong policy id from a wrong arity.

identitiesDeliberatelyUnmoved.title: Fraud-proof catalogue category order
identitiesDeliberatelyUnmoved.why: The receipt family is not a catalogue category, so no category id shifts and the catalogue root and every membership proof are untouched. Independently corroborated: the F20 reconciliation's bindingInventory.registeredCatalogueCategories measures 11, and the ABI gate reports core and sdk agreement EXACT at 11.

downstreamIdentitiesMovedByTheRenumberin.whatMoved: The catalogue root, all 11 category script hashes and all 11 membership proofs.
downstreamIdentitiesMovedByTheRenumberin.why: These are NOT blueprint hashes. The six watcher suites build one synthetic single-byte script per contract, keyed on the contract's POSITION in DEPLOYMENT_MANIFEST_V1_CONTRACT_NAMES. Removing the two receipt names shifted every fraud-proof contract two places down (fraudProofDoubleSpend 39 -> 37 … fraudProofInvalidSignature 54 -> 52), so every synthetic hash and therefore the whole catalogue changed. This is the clearest demonstration in the batch of why a positional vector's removals must be enumerated: nothing about the fraud-proof families changed, yet every one of their identities moved.
downstreamIdentitiesMovedByTheRenumberin.notMoved: FIXED_SCRIPT_CATALOGUE (one shared script hash) is position-independent and is correct unchanged. The category count stays 11.
downstreamIdentitiesMovedByTheRenumberin.derivedBy: buildFraudProofCatalogueDeploymentInfo(fraudProofsToIndexedValidators(...)) — the deployment producer itself, run over the same synthetic contract set the suites build. verifyDeploymentManifestV1FraudProofCatalogueIdentity re-checks canonical proof CBOR and membership at module load, so a transcription slip cannot survive import.
downstreamIdentitiesMovedByTheRenumberin.effect: Cleared the file-level 'No canonical watcher fraud-proof catalogue fixture matches the deployed scripts' failure from all six dependent watcher suites.

verification.gateHazard: demo/scripts/verify-canonical-v1-abi-freeze.mjs reads its identity sources from the GIT INDEX (`git show :<path>`, readIndexedText at line 105), not the working tree. On an uncommitted tree it therefore measures HEAD. Here that is actively deceptive: the default run reported ABI-01 cardinality 55 — the SAME number as the true post-purge value, because the certificate append (+2) and this removal (-2) cancel — while the digest differed (695a3f1d… index vs 0c841add… worktree). Verifying by cardinality alone yields a false green.
verification.committedEquivalentProof: The three residual gate failures (two aiken.toml compiler arms, one F20 reconciliation drift finding) were proved to be index artifacts rather than real drift by building a scratch index and re-running against it: `cp .git/index $TMP/probe.index && GIT_INDEX_FILE=$TMP/probe.index git add -A && GIT_INDEX_FILE=$TMP/probe.index node scripts/verify-canonical-v1-abi-freeze.mjs`. The real index was left untouched. Result: 'Canonical V1 ABI freeze verified. cross-package identities re-derived: 7/7; catalogue categories: 11, validator directories: 18; blueprint: 398 validators from v1.1.23+2a78108; drift findings: 0; waivers: 0.' All three resolve on commit.
verification.selfTest: demo/scripts/verify-canonical-v1-abi-freeze-self-test.mjs — PASS, 2 control runs accepted, 23 hostile mutations rejected. NOTE: this suite itself contained a latent vacuous mutation. Its 'understated ABI-01 cardinality' seed was hardcoded to 54 while the truth was 55; when this removal made 54 the TRUE value the seeded defect became a no-op and the gate accepted it — caught only because the self-test asserts that a rejection occurred at all. The seed is now derived (`cardinality -= 1`) with a numeric-agnostic expectation, so it cannot go vacuous again on a future cardinality change.

vacuousGateFoundAndClosed.surface: demo/midgard-validation/tests/complete-item-proof-fit-emulator-v1.test.ts — 'rejects substituted and trailing-byte items through the deployed reference route'
vacuousGateFoundAndClosed.finding: buildCanonicalDecodeItemCase selected the FIRST canonicalDecode + transactionFieldItem witness, which is field 0's, not field 2's. Its itemBytes parameter therefore had no relationship to the preimage the row measured. The consequence was that `substituted[itemBytes - 100]` wrote PAST THE END of a roughly 40-byte buffer and was a silent no-op: the 'substituted' preimage was byte-identical to the original, so the row asserted a rejection of something it had never actually altered.
vacuousGateFoundAndClosed.howItSurfaced: The row was initially triaged as a regeneration-moved pin ('resolved instead of rejecting'). Re-pinning it would have converted a rejection assertion into an acceptance assertion and cemented the vacuity permanently. It was caught because two workers cross-checked: one measured the failure, another diagnosed the selection defect independently.
vacuousGateFoundAndClosed.fix: Selection now requires fieldIndex === 2 AND fieldPreimage.length === encodeMidgardFieldPreimageV1([item]).length; the substitution is keyed off substituted.length - 100 and guarded by assertions that the flip actually landed (length unchanged, equals(original) false). A test that mutates a buffer now proves the mutation took.
vacuousGateFoundAndClosed.outcome: The row genuinely rejects both the substituted and the trailing-byte publication. The property it exists to protect is real for the first time.
vacuousGateFoundAndClosed.noRegression: complete-item-proof-fit-v1.test.ts 5/5 and complete-item-carriage-tiers-emulator-v1.test.ts 4/4 remain green after the selection edit.
